authoritative_for: Email constructs and submits one caller-provided plain-text message with optional local attachments. It uses fixed addresses and owns bounded retries and command reporting.
Email owns use of a generated or caller-supplied idempotency key for the frozen Resend request and reports the message identifier returned on Resend acceptance.
not_authoritative_for: The caller owns send authorization, message meaning, product occurrence state, rendering, scheduling, and any supplied idempotency-key identity.
Resend owns submission acceptance and its external record, while Gmail owns final delivery, spam handling, and inbox receipt.

covers: All supported user-facing Email CLI outcomes for immediate plain-text submission with optional local file attachments to the product-fixed recipient in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, installation and release operations, drafting, previews, arbitrary recipients or senders, HTML, remote attachment URLs, copies, scheduling, queues, delivery tracking, and live external readiness are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Email is a local current-user CLI; its installed wrapper obtains only RESEND_API_KEY from the user's shell configuration and starts the payload with a scrubbed environment.
Catalog presence, command availability, and possession of an idempotency key do not authorize sending.
shared_privacy_and_retention: A real send discloses the exact subject, body, and any attachment filenames and bytes to Resend and Gmail and discloses any caller-supplied idempotency key to Resend.
Email retains no subject, body, attachments, API key, idempotency key, queue, or delivery history in local product state.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release identifies the installed bundle, while entry contract version identifies the supported send semantics.
No cross-release compatibility window, API deprecation period, or external-provider retention guarantee is promised beyond an entry's explicit declarations.
operational_limits: Email supports one synchronous immediate plain-text submission to fixed addresses per invocation and has no daemon, draft store, scheduler, queue, or final-delivery observer.
Submission requires a valid credential, network access, and Resend availability and policy acceptance. Gmail controls final delivery, which is outside Email success.
